title: Scroll long lists under restrictive style policies
goal: Use Virtualize without an inline-style exception.

selectionNotes: Strict style CSP; trusted CSSOM layout.

runtime.name: .NET
runtime.reason: Virtualize's numeric layout attributes require the .NET 11 renderer and matching browser code.

sdk.name: .NET SDK
sdk.reason: Use matching Web SDK/reference and Internal.Assets browser files; the RC2 pin reproduces this evidence.

language.name: C#
language.reason: Canonical current sample language mode; this migration itself requires no new C# syntax.

prerequisites: Use Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web, net11.0, nullable and implicit usings. Virtualize is in Microsoft.AspNetCore.App; no separate virtualization package, provider, account or workload is required. The pinned SDK resolves Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Internal.Assets 11.0.0-rc.2.26504.105.

Register Interactive Server, load matching blazor.web.js and allow the app's trusted boot script and local circuit connection. Put app styles in an allowed external stylesheet. The tested header enforces style-src 'self', style-src-elem 'self' and style-src-attr 'none'.

Use a real scroll container, fixed-height rows and browser IntersectionObserver/MutationObserver/CSSOM support. Execute the policy controls and inspect actual visible distant IDs in the consumer browser.
constraints: Virtualize; source-reviewed migration, browser evidence still needed for each consuming app. This sample supplies real Chrome evidence, not a universal CSP or browser certification.

Remove the virtualization-specific inline-style exception and any app-owned spacer rewrite only after upgrading both renderer and browser assets. Keep unrelated app/framework script, stylesheet and circuit requirements separate.

Numeric layout attributes are translated through CSSOM by trusted framework JavaScript. Resulting style attributes in the DOM are expected; their presence alone is not evidence of a CSP failure. This is not a prohibition on programmatic CSS.

The .NET 10 comparison executes Virtualize with an explicit style-src-attr 'unsafe-inline' exception and fails the strict negative control. It is not an older-target route for the newer rendering. Static SSR/prerender alone do not provide virtual scrolling; WebAssembly/Auto, other browsers/platforms and GA are unverified.

The loopback ws://localhost:* connect-src allowance is solely for local Interactive Server testing. Use the deployed application's actual secure circuit origin and independent script policy; no deployment policy audit is claimed.

evidence.scope: Actual pinned Web SDK build. Separate real Chrome execution compares the explicit attribute exception with the enforced strict failure, visible distant IDs and attribute/element/CSSOM controls; no mocks.

Actual pinned Web SDK build. Separate real Chrome execution checks strict response header, actual visible distant rows, bounded DOM window, return scrolling and enforced attribute/element controls without virtualization exceptions; no mocks.

humanProof.scope: Actual local Chrome/Interactive Server policy enforcement and visible scrolling were executed by the agent. Consumers still need their own browser/CSP checks; no external provider, other-browser or GA proof is claimed.
